skill.name: follow-up
skill.description: Creates concise follow-up emails that re-engage prospects with a clear new angle and one simple call to action.
skill.summary: Write concise follow-up emails for outreach, sales, and relationship building.
skill.author: humanizerai

security_audit.summary: The static external-command finding is a false positive caused by a Markdown output fence in SKILL.md lines 76-82. No executable code, prompt injection attempt, network access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged backticks are a Markdown code fence for the email output format, not Ruby or shell execution. SKILL.md contains prompt instructions only and no executable script.

content.value_statement: Unanswered outreach needs tactful persistence, not repeated messages. This skill creates short follow-ups with fresh value and one clear ask.
actual_capabilities: Drafts follow-up emails based on original outreach context.
Selects a strategy for first, second, or third follow-ups.
Applies bump, value-add, and breakup email frameworks.
Keeps messages short, scannable, and focused on one call to action.
Explains the framework used, the new angle, and the word count.
limitations: Does not send emails or connect to an inbox.
Requires enough original outreach context to write a useful message.
Does not verify prospect facts, news, or company details.
Cannot guarantee replies or legal compliance for outreach campaigns.

use_cases.title: Sales Prospect Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Create a short second touch after a prospect does not answer the first email.

use_cases.title: Partnership Outreach
use_cases.description: Re-engage a potential partner with a new angle, useful resource, or simpler ask.

use_cases.title: Recruiting Candidate Reminder
use_cases.description: Write a polite reminder that keeps the opportunity clear without adding pressure.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with simple outreach context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the follow-up skill. Original email: I introduced our analytics product to a VP of Sales. It has been four days. This is follow-up number one.

prompt_templates.title: Add New Value
prompt_templates.scenario: Second follow-up with a helpful new resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the follow-up skill for follow-up number two. Original context: I offered a customer onboarding audit. It has been nine days. New context: we published a checklist for reducing churn.

prompt_templates.title: Permission-Based Close
prompt_templates.scenario: Third follow-up before ending the sequence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the follow-up skill for follow-up number three. Original context: I invited a director to discuss vendor consolidation. It has been sixteen days. Make it a polite breakup email.

prompt_templates.title: Tailored Multi-Stakeholder Follow-Up
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with role, tone, and constraint details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the follow-up skill. Original context: I wrote to a finance leader about invoice approval delays. It has been eight days and this is follow-up number two. Add a concise benchmark insight, keep a professional tone, and ask for a fifteen-minute call.

output_examples.input: Follow-up number one after a product intro email sent four days ago.
output_examples.output:
Subject: Re: analytics visibility

Hi Maya,

Floating this back up with one extra thought. Teams usually find the fastest wins by checking where forecast updates lose context between sales and finance.

Would it be worth a brief look next week?

Jon

Framework used: The Bump
What is different: Adds a specific operational angle
Word count: 44

output_examples.input: Follow-up number two after offering an onboarding audit.
output_examples.output:
Subject: onboarding friction checklist

Hi Priya,

I saw several teams reduce early churn by reviewing the first seven customer touchpoints. I can share a short checklist that maps those gaps.

Would that be useful for your team?

Alex

Framework used: The Value-Add
What is different: Offers a useful resource
Word count: 49

output_examples.input: Follow-up number three after no reply to a partnership request.
output_examples.output:
Subject: should I close this out?

Hi Daniel,

I do not want to keep adding noise to your inbox. Should I close the loop on the partner pilot idea for now?

Thanks,
Sam

Framework used: The Breakup
What is different: Gives an easy opt-out
Word count: 35

best_practices: Provide the original email context, timing, and follow-up number.
Add a fresh detail, resource, or reason for the recipient to respond.
Review the final email for accurate names, facts, and tone.
anti_patterns: Do not resend the same message with a different subject line.
Do not add multiple calls to action in one follow-up.
Do not use guilt, pressure, or passive-aggressive wording.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates short follow-up emails with a subject line, body, framework note, difference note, and word count.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it write different follow-up numbers?
faq.answer: Yes. It adapts strategy for first, second, and third follow-ups.

faq.question: Does it send the email?
faq.answer: No. It only drafts the message for review and use in another email tool.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the original outreach context, days since the last email, follow-up number, and any new context.

faq.question: Can it replace legal or compliance review?
faq.answer: No. Review outreach against your company policy and applicable communication laws before sending.
